utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case Number IT-02-60-T, The Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. I apologise for the delay. But since we have the witness here, I'm not going to talk about it. Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Karnavas: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to pick up where we left off yesterday. If you recall, you had indicated that at one point on the 11th of July 1995, you were on your way back to get some supplies. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And could you please tell us, just so we can pick up from yesterday, where were you when you left off to go for the supplies?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were there near Kula, some 10 to 100 metres away, down the forest along our line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And where were the supplies, sir? Where were the supplies located?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were up there in the room where we came when we first came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And so when you went there, what did you see, if anything?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I went up there, packed it up. General Mladic was there. And there were some other officers there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise the other officers?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krstic, the general. But I was in a hurry because I didn't want Mr. Blagojevic to be alone down there. I didn't pay much attention, just what I could see at first glance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go up to General Mladic and General Krstic to salute them as you went for your supplies?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were -- they had their backs turned to me. At one point, the general happened to see me and called me, and he said, "How come you, little guy, are up here?" I went up. I said hello. He hugged me, gave me a hug. And I said that I was with Colonel Blagojevic. He gave me a hug. He said I shouldn't be afraid. And he said, "Well, where is he, where is Blagojevic?" And I told him he was down with me in the forest. And he said, "Didn't he go off to Srebrenica and does he know at all that he can enter, that it's free?" I made no comment. And he said once again, "Don't be afraid. You can take the message down to him quite freely. You can go down there. Because I've already sent the soldiers down. It's free. You can take the shortcut down there, and I'll be there at about 6.30 myself." That's what he said more or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, had you met General Mladic before?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not personally. I knew him, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So what did you do after that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I continued on my way down to Colonel Blagojevic and conveyed the message. So we didn't manage to have anything to eat at that point. He looked at me rather astonished and said, "Well, we should have gone down earlier. How can we down now that the others have left?" He took the map and had a look to find a route down there, and the spa was marked on the map, the one down below near Srebrenica, and there was a path leading down there, a shortcut. However, we -- it seemed that we had chosen the worst terrain to climb down. It was very steep. And I had to sort of rush down. It was all we could do to reach the bottom. I had injuries on my legs, and my boots were very tight, and I found it very difficult to climb down. But somehow we did manage to reach that spa at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then what happened when you reached the spa?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There really were soldiers there, ours. Everything was really peaceful and quiet. They were moving around. And we continued to walk around down there. We just said hello and went on towards the centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did any soldiers come with you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far did you get down that day, on the 11th?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We got down to the school, and we sat down to have a rest there on the steps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is the school?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps halfway, so in the middle of Srebrenica. Actually I didn't know Srebrenica from before, but I would say it was somewhere in the middle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Who did you see when you got there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the soldiers were there, quite a lot of them. Some army, but I didn't know who they were, although it was our army, but I didn't know any of the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak with any of them?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Colonel Blagojevic speak with any of them?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you do?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We set out. And as I didn't have a signal, I wasn't getting a signal because it was like a big depression, and I had to find a spot where I could get my signal and call up the brigade command to come and get us. But I wasn't able to get a signal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were you able ever to get a signal?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From there, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, we went down to the playground, I think. I found it very hard to walk because I had sores on my feet from the boots and from climbing down the hill. So I did my best to find a connection, a signal. And the colonel said, "We'll go straight ahead and if someone turns up, if a car turns up, they might be able to give us a lift if we're lucky." But as I say, I really couldn't walk any more, my feet hurt. And I sat down to find a signal, but I wasn't able to get one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said that you were by the playground. Could you please tell us where the playground is located, if you know.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was towards the end of Srebrenica, the very centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if you were coming into Srebrenica from Bratunac or Potocari, that would be the entrance of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you had come in through the other way, from the other direction?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So in which direction were you walking? Were you walking back into the centre of Srebrenica or were you walking towards Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were walking towards Potocari because we were on our way to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about what time was it, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what the time was. But it wasn't dark yet, to towards evening. Before dusk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, how far did you walk?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not far. We stopped somewhere there, and I was looking for a signal, as I've already said. But the colonel called out to me. Colonel Blagojevic said, "Don't waste time trying to find a signal. They're not going to let us pass anyway, so we can't pass."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So why did he say that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. There must have been some soldiers there, a checkpoint of some kind. And they wouldn't allow anybody to pass by. They said that we couldn't go further down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did a car ever come by?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I said -- no, I said, never mind. And I didn't know there was a side road. However, a vehicle did come by. I didn't know what it was. It was moving around town. And the colonel called out to me and said, "Come on, we'll go with him. Come on, lad. We'll go with him." And then we took the side road to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. In which direction was the car heading? In which direction was the car heading initially when it was stopped? Or the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But in which direction was this vehicle heading when you first saw it? Was it going towards Srebrenica, towards the other end, or was it heading towards Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And at what point did you get into the car?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all I saw was that the car was turning round on the road. And at that point, the colonel called out to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Once you got into the car, or in this vehicle -- and let's figure out first of all what kind of a vehicle is it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a heavy-duty vehicle of some kind. But how shall I explain this to you? I was not -- I was tired. I was exhausted. Looked terrible. I didn't pay much attention. I just got in and said, "Thank goodness I don't have to go on foot." But anyway, it was a heavy-duty vehicle of some kind. I didn't know the driver. We didn't speak a single word in the car until we reached Bratunac and the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you got into this vehicle, in which direction was the vehicle going towards, when you got in?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, right where we were, not far off from there, there was a road of some kind. And it was -- it led across a hill. And it was a sort of round-about route, a byroad that we took from Srebrenica, Potocari. We circumvented that whole area and went further up. I don't know what the road was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any attempt to go through Potocari while you were in this vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what are the lighting conditions at this point in time when you get into this vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by "lighting conditions".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you didn't have a watch on, you said, so we don't know what time it is. So I'm asking you if you could tell us what the lighting conditions were so that we know perhaps about what time it might have been. So do you recall what the lighting conditions were when you got into this vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. How long had you been in Srebrenica at this point in time before you got into the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps about an hour. The amount of time we needed to go down, go through Srebrenica, and look for some transport. So one to two hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that period while you were in Srebrenica, did you see any officers?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was only when we got in down there and passed by both sides. Behind us, you could hear, and I saw -- caught a glimpse of General Mladic and some others in a group with him. I wasn't able to recognise who was there exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was General Mladic doing?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. He was shouting at some soldiers. That's what you could hear. Because you could hear a voice shouting, so we looked up to see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was Colonel Blagojevic at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was next to me, perhaps a metre or two away from me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where exactly in Srebrenica, if you know, were you located? Sir, where exactly were you when you saw General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were on one side of the department store looking towards, in the direction of -- or rather, down Srebrenica. We would be on the right. And Mr. Mladic and the others were on the left-hand side behind the department store, more or less in front of the municipality building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's the name of the department store?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. It just said department store, "robna kuca."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the distance between where you were located and General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps 50-odd metres, maybe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Colonel Blagojevic's response when he saw General Mladic, or his reaction?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, nothing. He just turned round, took a look, and continued on his way, and of course I did the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go in the direction where General Mladic was?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now I thought you told us that General Mladic had instructed you to tell Colonel Blagojevic that he would see him in Srebrenica around 6.30 in the afternoon. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you pass that message on to your commander?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at that point in time, when you saw General Mladic, your commander knew or would have known from your conversation with the commander that General Mladic expected to see him. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you remind your commander that General Mladic wanted to see him and perhaps the two of you should go and greet the general?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't need to. He'd already seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In which direction did you and your commander go in relation to where General Mladic was heading at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Mladic wasn't moving around. He wasn't heading anywhere. He was just standing around with this group, and we went towards town, towards the centre of town, because it was the very entrance to Srebrenica, the way we had come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you did that, did you do it in a manner in which or -- did you take a route where at least General Mladic could see the two of you, that you were both in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, except that we turned when we came to the school, made a turn and had a rest there. I'm not sure that he could have seen us there. Perhaps not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see General Mladic after that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time did you get into town? Back to Bratunac, after you got into this car?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was dusk, perhaps 9.00, half past 8.00, 9.00, I'm not quite sure. But this was judging by the atmospheric conditions, not by the watch. So it had begun to be dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did it take you to get back from -- to get back to Bratunac from the time that you got into this vehicle? How long did it take you, in light of the route that you took?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I thought it might have been an hour. An hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this an asphalt road that you took?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to begin with. We went across a hill first, but then afterwards we reached an asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us -- can you recount the route that you took from Srebrenica back to Bratunac? Do you know the location?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on, I realised, I think it went up until -- up by the Sase mine. It's like going round in a circle, in circles. You pass by all these places, and then you emerge on Bratunac territory from that other side, the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this way, you bypassed Potocari completely?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We bypassed it quite a bit. We took the route in quite the opposite direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that your legs and your feet had been hurting. At one point, did you come across any horses?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was there while we were waiting at the playground, and Colonel Blagojevic said to me that we would continue on foot. And if we got down to the bottom, we might be picked up by a car. And I made a joke and said, "Colonel," because there were four or five horses over there and they were in harness. And I made a joke, perhaps I could take a horse and help me along because I had all my gear on me. He just looked at me and said, "Don't let me catch you doing anything like that, anything of the kind." Although I did sort of make a joke of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, once you got back to Bratunac, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we got down to Bratunac, the brigade command, and the young guy left us there and went back. And I found it very hard to get out of the car because I had grown cold and stiff, and it was all I could do to reach the command. I gave back my equipment that was issued to me. I reported to the komandir and said I would be at home because I had to take a rest. And I said good-bye to the colonel there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice any officers over there from any other units when you got out of the car or out of this vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you let off once you got to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I say, he brought us to in front of the entrance of the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go inside the building at that point?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got into the building -- incidentally, where is your office?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in the building? You want me to describe that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please. We know there's a right entrance. We know there's a left entrance, we know there's a ground floor, and we know there's a first floor. So if you could tell us where was your office in that building?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had an office not in that building, but there was an auxiliary, an annex building where we had our equipment. And they were the maintenance men there on duty there, like me. So we would leave our equipment there and pick it up from that point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that wasn't the building where the military police were stationed in, was it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you got to this auxiliary building, did you notice any other officers, higher echelon officers, or officers from other units?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From there, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps some 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from there, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went home then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is your home?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nearby, about two kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which direction? Towards Ljubovija, towards Kravica, or towards Potocari? Which direction?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not towards any of these. It wasn't in any of these directions. It was in the fourth direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which direction is that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The direction we had come from when we were going toward Bratunac by car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when was the next -- when was the next time that you reported -- reported into the Bratunac Brigade for duty?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the next day, I reported, and they could see that I couldn't walk. I said if it was absolutely necessary, I could be on duty at the command, and they said, "No, don't worry. Go home and have a rest. Take at least seven days' leave." I couldn't even put my slippers on. I didn't leave my house. I couldn't walk for at least ten days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you reported, how did you report, though, the next day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By telephone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to Zepa when the Bratunac Brigade went there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where do you currently live?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where I did before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's in the Bratunac area?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you been there for the last five or six years or since the time that you left the -- since 1995, you lived in that area?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions. There maybe some questions from Mr. Stojanovic's lawyer. The Prosecution may have some questions, and I'm sure the Judges may have a question or two. I want to thank you very much. You may wish to put your pen away because it's a little distracting for some. I appreciate your interest. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. Mr. Lukic, do you have any questions for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will only have three short questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And with your permission, I would like to put those questions in B/C/S. It's easier for the witness to understand me as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Whatever language you feel is easier to use. But be sure to make a pause after each questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll do my best. Cross-examined by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will mention a number which should not confuse you. It's only for the record. Yesterday, on page 73, line 15, Mr. Karnavas asked you the following question. It concerned the centre at Kik, the intercept centre. On the same page, line 19, you said that coded messages were transported by courier and that these messages were taken to the corps. Do you recall your reply?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who carried these messages? Do you know the name of the courier?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While at Kik, did you sometimes see Lieutenant Colonel Jevtovic there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who at this intercept centre was the superior from the corps?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey, cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. McCloskey:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- how old you were in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 21, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you were speaking of the events between July 6th through about the 11th, I noticed many times you answered that you didn't recall. You didn't recall whether you'd received messages over your radio or you didn't recall whether you'd sent messages. Is it fair to say your memory of those days is not very good?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are referring to the messages I transmitted, I said that I remembered I hadn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you how -- so you could have received messages that you just don't remember. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that I did not receive any messages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Djordje Pejic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember seeing him around 10 and 11 July in the Pribicevac area?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present in what he has described as being the Pribicevac area where he was there on that hill with General Blagojevic and General Krstic, and General Krstic gave him an order to take him some kind of engineering machine and do some work with it down the hill? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Pejic has testified here that he was concerned about that job, and so he left the area briefly and called Colonel Blagojevic and spoke to him on the telephone and asked him about whether he needed to do that job or not. And he said that Colonel Blagojevic over the phone told him, yeah, he had to go do it. Do you remember any of that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what was your code name for your commander Blagojevic in your little radio centre that you were carrying around with you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I have to say that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not a secret any more. Don't worry about it. You don't have to, but it's really not a secret any more.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. Well, it's not a secret. But I was taught that. That's how I was trained

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you were taught not to tell the enemy anything about what you were doing. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it was "RUMA Jedan."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me show you something. It has been marked as P852. And if we could show him just the front page of the B/C/S version. And if we could put the English on the ELMO. This is something that the Office of the Prosecutor obtained. And it appears to be a work schedule for the radio network for an operation called Krivaja 95. And have you ever seen this before?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And here it says the code name for the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade is RUMA. And you had told us a similar name earlier. Is that what you remember the code name being, RUMA?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was in the brigade. And I was RUMA 1, or "jedan." And yes, all the papers I had were about RUMA, not about anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was Colonel Blagojevic's code name?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was RUMA 1, and I responded. But it was the same code name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were aware of the code names of the other units and posts on this list, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not aware of this. This may have been down there in the brigade, but I never carried this on me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you would have needed to know the code names of, say, for example, the forward command post of the Drina Corps at Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But my komandir didn't give me anything, really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think Colonel Blagojevic would have gone into combat without knowing any of the code names of the units in his command post? Is that what you're saying? Military secrets are over now. You're testifying under oath.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm only speaking the truth. I'm telling you honestly. But whether Colonel Blagojevic went into combat or not, I don't know. But those were the orders I had. And I had only that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you a map that -- just to help us a bit with some of the areas you've talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This has been marked as P858. And if we could also -- we could put it on the ELMO. And if you could centre on the ELMO the -- what is marked as Pribicevac. That should do it. And this, Your Honours, is a 1:25.000 scale map. It's a little bigger than the 1:50.000 maps that we've usually seen. So each of those squares should be a kilometre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, do you see marked on this map the little village of Pribicevac with -- it has got little buildings marked around it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the building that you stayed in in that little cluster or in that area of buildings somewhere? It may not be the exact building. Don't worry about that. I'm just asking you the general area. Is that where the building was?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Somewhere in the centre. I'm not quite sure, but yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've spoken of a little hilltop area at Kula. Was there an observation area up there on that hilltop at Kula where people frequently went? Is this, in fact, where you talked about going to?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We would go there from time to time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you point -- just point that out for us so we -- I mean, I think we can all see it. But just to make sure we're on the --

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And that was a little bare hilltop that -- where you could look right down into the valley and see Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I couldn't see anything, but I didn't really look. Probably you could see something. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just asked you if you could look down and see Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us you can't stand on that bare hilltop and look right down and see the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was standing some 50 metres in front of the trenches. Maybe you could see down if you went behind the line, but I didn't dare do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've described going up to Kula with your commander several times over those days. And so when you went up to Kula, you went up to take a look around, didn't you? That's what that observation post was for, so it could overview the battle scene.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was a table in front of the trenches. We sat there. And the people in the trench would make us coffee. We didn't look at a battlefield. There was no battlefield there. We simply sat there. My task was to establish a communication, to man my equipment, to be close to my equipment all the time. So I sat there at the table, and I didn't really have any need to walk around and look about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've said that your commander, Blagojevic, went up to Kula several times, Kula being, as we can see, the top, the little bare knoll. Didn't you go up there with him?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look here, he was there, but it's not really such a high elevation. We sat at that table. There was nowhere to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you went up to Kula with your commander, to the top of that little hill several times over those days?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you never looked down towards Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I would look towards Srebrenica, but there were trees. What was there to see but trees?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can see a good part of Srebrenica from the top of that hill. There's no trees. It's a bare hill, and it's a high elevation. You look right down into the town. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see it. Really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you never saw any of the shell detonations in town on the 9th, 10th, 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who the commander of the 3rd Battalion is? Mr. Zekic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- were you present with Mr. Blagojevic when Mr. Zekic reported to him personally on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know Mr. Zekic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did any officers -- do you remember any officers reporting to Colonel Blagojevic on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for reporting, that can take a few minutes. And I didn't say I was stuck to Colonel Blagojevic. I had to go to the toilet, to fetch water, or I may simply have dozed off for half an hour. So something like that could have happened. But I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that certainly officers could have reported and communicated with Colonel Blagojevic and you didn't know about it because you weren't stuck with him every minute?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was only for brief periods that I was absent to go to the toilet or to fetch water. But he could have needed to establish communications, but he didn't ask me to call the brigade or anybody else. I don't think he had anything to hide from me. But I never noticed or observed him talking to anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where he slept each night from 6th July through 11th July? Let me say through 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He slept there in that building where we were the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware if General Krstic went back to Bratunac each evening those days?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're sure Colonel Blagojevic did not go back to Bratunac on those evenings?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm sure that he didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have every single meal that you ever ate from 6 July through 11 July with Colonel Blagojevic? Breakfast, lunch, dinner?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, our needs for food were different. I had two meals; he had three meals a day. Or I had one meal and he had two. We didn't eat together. He would eat or I would eat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were many times where he had meals without you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many times. But as I said, we didn't have a predetermined schedule as to when we would both eat. But he took his food there. He didn't go somewhere, to a restaurant. He stayed there to eat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a little video, just ask you a couple of questions about it. And if you see anything you recognise, you can tell us as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise anybody in that photo?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that equipment on the back of that fellow's back?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I carried something similar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what is that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see properly. I'm not sure, but it reminds me of the RUP that I carried.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe we'll get a better look at it. Let's just keep going. Is that an RUP?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if this person was one of the units in the Srebrenica operation, could you have -- and you had his frequency and his call sign, could you have spoken to this person on your RUP?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depended on the configuration of the terrain. If it was within range to my network and if I knew the frequency, then yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this person in this black uniform or black jumpsuit wearing this RUP?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can get a better look now. Do you recognise that guy?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know who that is on this still shot?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And is that a Motorola that he's speaking into in his right hand?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, take a look at what's in his left hand, and let's play the video a bit.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A receiver of some kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in his left hand, is that the same kind of a phone device that a RUP-12 or another kind of radio might have? And right now, we can see this big RUP-12-looking antenna that's sticking out as well.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it looks like it, but I'm not sure because I can't see the actual device.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Maybe we can get a better look. Let's just watch it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's from P21.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the kind of radio traffic you could hear during these days, 6 July through 11 July?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean. Was that what?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your radio was on, I take it, during 6 July through 11 July, your RUP, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you listened to various channels and frequencies during that time, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't listen to any traffic at all?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't listen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You couldn't have your radio on and hear what that guy was saying, for example, if you listened on the same frequency and the same channel?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had the KZ encryption protection, and I could only talk to the brigade command with this KZ system. So in that case, they would have had to change the key. I would have had to go to Bratunac, had the key changed, and then I might have a chance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could people call you on your RUP-12 and speak to you over the open airwaves?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were completely out of communication, then? Your radio was -- you couldn't be contacted?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did have a connection to whom I was subordinated. So myself and Colonel Blagojevic, we had a connection with the people down there at the brigade. And I had to change the key, receive the codes if I wanted to hear, and have communication with the other units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you could only receive encrypted communications from the brigade during this time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The tone was clear. But if somebody else wasn't able to follow us -- there was no reception on our part. That's why the KZ system was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could someone from the forward command post while you and the colonel were at the top of the hill at Kula, could someone call you on the radio and speak to you without encryption?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you or Blagojevic have a Motorola?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the only way anyone could ever get in touch with Blagojevic was by courier or by person or by an encrypted message. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, more or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any redirect, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This cross calls for no redirect, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, at this stage, are there any documents to tender? Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I think the communications plan which was P852 and just the small map that we used, P858.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, the communication plan, Your Honour, I fail to see how this comes in, on what foundation it comes in. It was pointed to the gentleman, he looked at it, he recognised the code name. But other than that, there was no other foundation. And there's a bunch of information in this that has been translated that we don't know who is it from, what relevance it might have, and it might have some prejudicial value to this case and no probative. So unless I can hear some more argument on it, I would -- I don't think it should be admitted. As for the map, I welcome the introduction of this map. And if we could have some more maps of that size, I think it would be nice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey, would you please lay some foundations for Document P852.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. I think the most significant from what we've seen is that it roughly matches the code name that this witness has spoken to, so it does provide us information. It's also a document that was obtained during the -- and I'll have to double check this, but I'm almost sure it was obtained during the search of the -- in fact, it is. It was obtained along with the other materials from the search of the Bratunac Brigade. It was dealt with quite a bit in the Krstic case. It was a Krstic exhibit. And Defence have had it, you know, forever. And it's basically a list of codes and units and phrases that -- military phrases that are coded so you don't have to alert the enemy what you're saying. You can just say, you know, the code name or the code number for it. It's a good listing, I think, of the units involved in the operation and would be helpful for the Court to have, as well as, of course, it relates directly to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: This document is only related to the Bratunac Brigade, and not the Zvornik Brigade, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It is actually what we believe is the Drina Corps communications plan for Krivaja 95. It is a -- it should be seen in conjunction with the Krivaja 95 plan. You can see on the front of it, it makes specific reference to "strictly confidential, Krivaja 95." And so it's normal for a Drina Corps-type operation to have a communications plan. And so you can see that the Bratunac Brigade is listed as one of the users in the communication schedule. But so are all the other units that we know that have already been mentioned by various witnesses to be involved in this attack. The forward command post, the Zvornik Brigade; the 2nd Romanija Brigade, that was Mr. Trivic's; the Birac Brigade, that's Sveto Zarandric; Milici, that's Nastic; Vlasnica. So it's a corps-wide plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, this Bench believes that this document is relevant to this case, and in this particular witness it goes to the credibility of this witness. And it has some probative value. So those two documents, P852, and the map, P858, are admitted into the evidence. It is so decided. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. After we're adjourned, the usher will show you out of the room. We wish you a pleasant journey back home. The hearing is adjourned and will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please stand up and make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I guess it's still good morning, sir. Would you please tell us what your name is.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Milos Loncarevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us your last name letter by letter.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: L-o-n-c-a-r-e-v-i-c.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Loncarevic. Could you please tell us where you're from.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: From Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you grow up?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: In Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us a little bit about your educational background.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I completed the chemical technical vocational school in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what year was that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: And I went to Italy to specialise in ceramics. 1989. That was my specialisation term. And my secondary school education in 1968.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you do your JNA service?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In 1968 in Virovitica in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you receive any training when you were with the JNA, specialised training?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, not specialised. I was a radio operator, signalsman, that kind of thing, in communications for the artillery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you mobilised at the outbreak of the war in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Not at the very beginning, but yes, I was mobilised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to being mobilised, could you please tell us what was your occupation and what you were doing in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Before mobilisation, I was the production manager in the factory for ceramic tiles in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the name of that factory?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: It is the name of Kaolin Bratunac ceramics factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As the production manager, could you please tell us a little bit about what that entailed, your job?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was responsible for the overall production line in the whole ceramic tile factory. I was the number one man in the production area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whether you were supervising anyone, and if so, how many?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Depending on the programmes we had --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please first slow down and then if you can repeat the number again of the employees.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As I was saying, depending on the output, there were approximately 460 workers in production.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell us the output of this factory so at least we have sort of an understanding of -- now that we know how many people you were managing, what sort of production you were outputting.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: It was like this. It was a factory, and its capacity was one of the biggest in Europe, in fact, in the 1980s. It was the third-largest factory in the world of that kind. The surface area of the factory itself was two and a half hectares, and it was under one roof. And the annual production was two and a half million square metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of tiles?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two and a half million square metres of what?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, tiles. Tiles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, was this factory working during the war?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, we couldn't organise the production line properly because it requires a continuous manufacturing process. Let me just tell you that to heat up the tunnel furnaces, for example, you would need a cycle of 21 days, and as much to have the furnaces cooled down. So that I had to go around collecting up workers from the villages, but I wasn't able to ensure that level of production.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you can just please tell us the layout of this factory compound so we have some understanding of the space of it. How many buildings are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, the overall factory was under one roof, two and a half hectares of it, under just one single roof. All that was separate, but also under this one roof was the administrative building where the command was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Was there a parking area?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: There was a parking area for privately owned vehicles outside this general compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that the administration building was attached to this -- or was one -- it was part of the factory. Could you please tell us, what was the administration building being used for during the war?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: The administration building was used as the command, the right-hand area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now -- and we're going to get to that later on when we get to the sketch of the building itself. But let me ask you, we have heard testimony that there was a small building or a shack or what have you in front of the factory that was being used by the military police.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But that belonged to decorative ceramics. It didn't actually belong to the Kaolin factory. It was outside the gates and the Kaolin compound, in front of the reception area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, from listening to your answer, am I correct in stating that the factory itself was -- that there was a gate and a fence or some sort of a wall surrounding the factory?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to focus your attention to the period of -- first, we're going to start from 1992 to 1995, just very briefly, if you could tell us when you were mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was mobilised at the beginning of May and distributed in the Territorial Defence as the factory had been stopped. I took out the gas that existed because there was the danger of bombing and that the bombing would set fire to it, to the gas, because the basic fuel for the production of ceramic tiles was propane, butane gas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were mobilised, where were you mobilised and what was your function?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I was deployed up at the line at Paici as an ordinary soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did a time come when you became a member of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: That was later because I was redeployed to the famous Kunjerac area, and there was an attack at Kunjerac every second or third day, and it was a difficult position to be assigned to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was before the establishment of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Before, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's skip that part and let's get to when you were mobilised with the Bratunac Brigade or when you became a member of it. Could you please tell us where -- in what unit you were serving.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Sometime in September in 1993, as chance would have it, I was not in the truck where nine soldiers were killed on the way to Kunjerac, nine individuals. I think five soldiers and three women were killed. And I left that unit and went back to my company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Which company were you in at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: At that time, or the one I went to? I wasn't in a single company when I left the Territorial Defence at Kunjerac at that position there. For a time, I was in the company -- I mean in the factory in the enterprise without any position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me fast-forward to July 1995. Would you please tell us whether you were with the Bratunac Brigade in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which unit were you serving in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I was in the rocket unit, the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long had you been in the rocket unit?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: From September 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And so from September 1993 to July 1995, and perhaps onwards, you're with the -- in this rocket unit. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, until July 1995 because I was demobilised later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you please tell us what position you held in July 1995 in this rocket unit.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I was the komandir of the squad of that rocket unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us in which company or in which battalion of the Bratunac Brigade this rocket unit belonged to?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: None. As far as I know, no company or unit. We were independent, as far as I know, because before me there was another komandir of that unit, and I inherited the unit from him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you take any orders at any point in time from Mico Gavric?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do know Mico Gavric, do you not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you please tell us where this rocket unit was located back in July 1995 concretely.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: The rocket unit was located in the compound of the Javor company, Javor Bratunac, it was a warehouse for building construction material, one kilometre away from the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going in which direction?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: In the direction of Ljubovija, Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that would be the opposite direction from Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please tell us for how long the unit had been located there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: It was located there throughout, before I arrived to join it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us how many men were in this unit?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Seven.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what sort of training did you and your men get to be in this rocket unit?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know to set off the rockets if you needed to use them at any given time?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, they were devices that we had seen. We saw these launchers in Bijeljina, for example, on one occasion. We saw them once, but it's not a device that you need any special schooling to operate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were the members of these -- you don't have to give us the actual names, but what sort of folk comprised this unit, this rocket unit?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, this is how it was: Mostly people, some were more important for the Bratunac Municipality, personages well known about town, if I can put it that way. There was an electrical engineer, for example. There was a machine engineer. I was the director of the factory. There was another director from the distribution side, distribution department. Then there was a driver. He had a father and brother up at the line, front lines. And so that was it. Mostly people who wanted to get away from the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us how close to the front line this rocket unit was located.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: About four kilometres I would say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From September 1993 to July 1995, prior to the events concerning Srebrenica, would you please tell us how much action your rocket unit saw; combat action, that is.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Almost nothing. We didn't see any action because we had very few rockets. We had a very small quantity, and those were 70-millimetre calibre rockets on the trailer. The launchers we had on the truck, we didn't use because the rockets were out of order. These were 57-millimetre rockets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I want to go into great detail as far as what you had available. But just first, before we get to that, could you please describe to us what you were doing, what you and your unit were doing, from September 1993 to July 1995? How did you spend your time there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you, we sat around, we were on duty. We drank brandy and coffee because we were a well-off unit as far as materiel goods were concerned. So the lower-ranking officers who came from the command, we could offer them a drink.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Where did you stay at night? Did you have facilities there for you to sleep?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No. We would spend the nights at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How close were you to your house?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: My house was a hundred metres away. Not just me, but the whole unit would go, and only one person would remain on duty who could call us on the phone if necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of means of communication did you have there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, the usual city telephone line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with this telephone line, could you be -- could you contact the Bratunac Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Through the communications centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you communicate with, for instance, Pribicevac where the 3rd Battalion had its command post or where, during the days in Srebrenica --

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, through the communications centre again. But we didn't contact. I don't know, I didn't call anyone then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say through the communications centre, what are you speaking of?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, that was the communications centre, the people working in the command who were making sure there were communications with those battalions and those units there. They had a telephone switchboard there. It belonged to my company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But directly, from where you were located, could you directly place a call, for instance, to Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about to your house?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You can only call numbers in Bratunac, nowhere else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's talk about what equipment this rocket unit had that you were the komandir of around July 1995. Could you please describe to us the various rockets, artillery, mortars, what have you, that were available to you.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: We had 57-millimetre launchers that were out of order because we didn't have rockets that were in good order that could be fired. On the truck, the truck was a 110 TAM, and there was a trailer on which the launchers were mounted. These were 70-millimetre launchers. And for those, we did have rockets, but only a small amount. These were American-made rockets which we called Mickey Mouse, and they were 70-millimetre rockets. We also had a grenade launcher on a truck. It was a TAM 150 truck, and these were 50 kilogram grenades. We had seven of them altogether, and that was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, operational at that point in time, July 1995, what did you have?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: We had 70-millimetre launchers and seven 50-kilogram grenades, and that was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much launchers did you have? How many 70-millimetre launchers did you have?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Two launchers of 12 rockets each. We used to refer to them as two honeycombs, and these were taken off a helicopter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm going to use as a reference date July 6th as the date when the activities around Srebrenica began; July 11th, as the date when Srebrenica fell. Would you please tell us whether on the day that the activities began concerning Srebrenica, July 6th, that you were on duty on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was on duty every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, prior to the activities commencing on July 6th, had you received any particular orders from anyone?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on July 6th, were you aware that activities were ongoing concerning Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what point -- did you ever become aware that Srebrenica or the forces that were within Srebrenica were being attacked?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I did become aware from the people in the communications centre who told us that on the phone. But I didn't believe it. I heard about it, but I didn't believe it. I didn't really take it seriously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you take it seriously?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: It was unimaginable for us that Srebrenica could be taken, in view of the numbers of men we had and the number of people and soldiers who were in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your location, could you hear the activities?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see the activities?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you asked to move your unit to any particular location at the commencement of these activities?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm going to go through from the 6th to the 11th and ask you day by day what your activities were. On the 7th, did you receive any orders to carry out any activities?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you carry out any activities anyway, without orders, on your own?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the 8th? Is there anything different?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No. No, not until the 11th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So the 9th and the 10th, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Nothing, right. All the days were the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you please tell us during that period, from the 6th to the 11th, we're going to talk about what happened on the 11th, but if you could tell us from the 6th to the 11th whether any other units showed up where you were located to perhaps assist in any way.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No. It's a small area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any additional materiel assistance, rockets and what have you, in the event --

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they send any special personnel with some specialised training that might assist in shooting off any rockets that might be called upon?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No. We were in a room that was perhaps nine square metres in size. And we had a warehouse or hangar where we could park two trucks and that was all the unit had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you spend those days any differently than you had spent the previous two years or so from September 1993 to July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: The day was the same as the previous one altogether. We played cards; we drank a drop or two of brandy, had coffee, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any officers from the Bratunac Brigade come by?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No, not any important ones. Some did drop in, lower-ranking officers, to take shelter for a while or to have a beer or to have a drink.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody from the Drina Corps, any higher-echelon officers from the Drina Corps or the Main Staff come by?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's move to July 11th. July 11, I take it from your previous answer, this day was slightly different than the 6th, the 7th, the 8th, the 9th, and the 10th.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what happened on that day.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: On the 11th, and please don't hold me to the time very precisely because I'm elderly and I've had an accident, so I'm quite confused about some things. But I remember well that it was at 10.00 that the duty man called me. I don't know what his name was. And he said that I should send a truck with grenades to Pribicevac and that General Mladic had issued this command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me stop you here. I want to go step by step. Now, where did you receive this call from? You said the duty officer. Who are we speaking about?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. From the communications centre, somebody from the communications centre, the duty officer, by I don't remember what his name was, and I didn't even know the names of all the duty officers there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that would be from the Bratunac Brigade communications centre?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the request was for you to send a truck to Pribicevac pursuant to an order that had been -- that was being passed on from General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they ask you what kind of truck you needed to send up there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The one carrying the grenade launcher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. How many trucks of those did you have?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the operational condition of this truck?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was in good condition. It was a truck like any other. And we only had seven grenades from the beginning to the end -- not from the beginning because the truck -- or rather the grenade launcher was produced in 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the truck itself functioned well?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the grenade launchers, had you at least test-fired them at some point in time from 1993 to 1995 to know whether they were operational?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On one occasion, but I wasn't there. Two grenades were tested. One exploded, and the other one didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
