utterances.text: Because these grenades were at the airport near the Drina where there was flooding, so they had been in the water. And probably they had got wet. But I'm no expert. I can't really tell you the real reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you send the truck to Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, along with the driver, did you send anyone else?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, three other crew members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you -- did it have grenades with it, or did you just send the truck?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the grenades were always on the truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All seven of them?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: All seven, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't keep any for reserve?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No. We always carried what we had. They were always on the truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, from your location to Pribicevac, how long would -- how long of a drive would that be in light of the conditions of the road and the terrain and the route that they would have to take?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: It could have got there in about two hours approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you ever see that truck again that day, the truck with the grenade launchers?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the evening when it came back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you notice when that truck came back?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: What could I have noticed? All the grenades were on the truck, which means it hadn't been used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can I conclude that you counted the grenades?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak with the members of the unit that you had sent up?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And did they give you a briefing or debriefing as to what had happened up in Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: They didn't see anything. It was far away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, do you know whether they had been ordered in any way by anyone to carry out any activities?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Nobody gave me such an order. Let me clarify: As a rule, we didn't shoot over the lines of our men. This was not secure. And the soldiers had already set out, so it was unsafe to shoot over the heads of our own men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why would that be unsafe?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, these motors carrying the grenade had been taken off some planes and had been damaged in the process. So sometimes it would happen that a grenade would go off -- fly off in the wrong direction, and you could never be absolutely sure what direction it would go in. And that was the reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall about what time the truck returned to the unit?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: At around 2000 hours, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask the men by any chance whether they had received any orders or had made any contact with any officers up in Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No. They all went to Pribicevac. I don't know who they reported to. But they came to Pribicevac, and they knew where the firing position was approximately because somebody up there showed them. They directed them. I don't know who. And they were there until they were told to go back and that was all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So this call comes in around 10.00. You send off the truck after 10.00 or so in the morning on July 11th. Does anything else happen on that day? Anything unusual that hadn't happened in the previous two years?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. At around 1800 hours, there was another call from the communications centre, and an order was issued that the truck with the launchers should go to the Zagoni position because as the duty officer told us, from the direction of Pale, it had been observed that the Muslims were not respecting certain agreements and that they were moving from Bjeceva toward Bratunac and that we were to go to that firing position in order to prevent a breakthrough of Muslims from Pale towards Zagoni and Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you recall with whom did you speak at the communications centre?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No. I don't know who the man was. I knew all the people in the communications centre by voice and by name, but I can't recall now who the duty officer was at the time. Usually, when they were using the switchboard, the operator would first speak, and I would recognise his voice. And then he would switch over to the duty officer in the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this individual at the command centre, the duty officer, whoever he was, was he in a position to issue you orders, to give you orders?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So was it his order, the duty officer? Was he ordering you to do this, or had he received an order from anyone and was just passing it on? Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: His words were, "The commander, General Mladic, is at a meeting in Fontana. The agreement is not being respected. Go to the firing position and prevent the Muslims from advancing toward Bratunac." It was something to that effect anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So this was not the duty officer's order, but he was relaying an order that had been given to him from General Mladic, if I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm telling you what I was told. I don't know. The duty officer said it was General Mladic's order. That's how it was transmitted to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you received that order, or this transmission of an order, did you contact your own commander, Colonel Blagojevic, to see whether you should carry out the order that had been given to you from the communications centre?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a reason why?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: The duty officer was the person in command at that point in time. I think that's how it was in the army, according to the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you relocate?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us how long -- what preparations you made, if any, before you moved to the position that you were told to go to?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: The rockets were already on the truck. We got to 10 metres below the firing position. We put 10 rockets in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Let me go step by step.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much time did it take you to prepare before you could leave to go to the location?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: The rockets were on the truck, so we could set out right away toward the firing position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long would it take you to get to the firing position?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: 15 or 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once you're there, how long would it take you to set up so you could carry out any firing, if necessary?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps about 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you, in fact, when you go there, carry out any firing?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: But I have to tell you before that, that it was then that I saw a vast number of people in Potocari, and I was terrified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We're going to go step by step. When you got to that location, at some point I will show you -- we will go through the map, but when you got to the location that you were told to go to, could you please describe to us what you were able to observe.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: When I got to the location, I noticed a huge mass of people. I didn't know who these people were. But we had heard that Srebrenica had fallen, and we saw a huge crowd of people in the part of Potocari that was visible from that position. And truth to tell, I was afraid of that huge crowd of people because at that time in Bratunac, there were only women and children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. First of all, what is the distance from where you were located to where the crowd was?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: About three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any way of identifying who was in Potocari? Did you have any binoculars?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No. You could just see the shapes of people. That was all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that point in time, were you able to see the makeup of the crowd, whether they were armed soldiers, women, children, elderly men?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No, no. At a distance of three kilometres, you can't see that with the naked eye.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you could see that these were human beings?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please tell us what you did once you got there, after you noticed this crowd.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: As I've already said, I said to shorten the range of the rockets towards Djeco [phoen] because I didn't know where the positions were, where our army's positions were and where the Serb soldiers were and the Muslims soldiers were. I didn't know where anybody else was. And then he fired 10 shells, 10 rockets, to stop the group from advancing to Bratunac, the group that was on the move.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please tell us whether the firing of these rockets were in the direction of the crowd of people that you had seen?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No, it's quite on the other side. The people were on quite the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what the range of these rockets are. What sort of range do they have?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Nine kilometres, 9.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from your location if you wanted to hit that crowd, you would have been able to with the range?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I must tell you that it was not the kind of weaponry that targets a target. It covers the terrain broad-based, disperses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So in other words, what you're telling us is not only did you have the range, but because of the way it hits the target you could have easily hit that crowd of people?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's not what the witness had said earlier. That's a misstatement of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, and let me quote: "It covers the terrain broad-based, disperses."

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I haven't asked a question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm just --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I can understand that the Prosecutor wishes to obstruct, but there's no need for this. I'm quoting from his previous answer, so I can lead him into the next question. It's not leading. I'm making sure that there is no mischaracterisation as I was accused of doing on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's an personal attack by the Prosecutor at this point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think you are prejudging the questions which have not been put on the table yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think they're prejudging, Your Honour. I haven't prejudged anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's hear the objections.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm just wondering if Mr. Karnavas can read the entire sentence, Your Honour. Because the first part of that was: "It was not the kind of weaponry that targets a target." And I think that's where the mischaracterisation occurred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that's a legitimate request.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just cut to the chase. I'll rephrase. Could you have hit that crowd from where you were standing given the range?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. I want to show you a map or part of a map, the best we can do under the circumstances. This is D150. If we can put this on the ELMO, it might need the technical assistance to sort of enlarge, zoom and enlarge. First of all, you notice that there is a date and what purports to be a signature on what is being shown as --

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- D150 for identification. Do you recognise that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you recognise it to be?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: It's the firing position, and the point that was targeted roughly. I made these markings and signed for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to go -- I'm told it's D151 for identification. Now, if you could please tell us, show us, I should say, where you were initially located, where your unit was located before and where did it go in order to carry out the firing? And you will need to go to the projector, sir. Bratunac is further up. There you go.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Bratunac towards Ljubovija. That's where it is roughly. If this is the Drina River, then it's round here. Bratunac towards Ljubovija and Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you could put an "X" over there, something that we overlooked to do yesterday. We'll get you something.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And from the "X", where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Along the road towards Jelovica and Zagoni. Bratunac, Jelovica, Zagoni.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's reflected with the "1"?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What is the "2" that's reflected on this map?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: The number "2" denotes the place that I was supposed to target.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it says there: "Pale."

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were you targeting that area?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, because it was from that area that the reconnaissance man who reported to the general had been seen, that the Muslims were starting along that road over Zagoni to Bratunac. So I shortened this distance on my own, half a kilometre towards Zagoni, because it's all forest land.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you shorten the distance?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know where our men were. And I wanted to stop people from advancing rather than killing them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you notice from your location a mass of people or anybody that was in the vicinity where you were targeting?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No, you couldn't see that. That was not visible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please draw a circle and a "3", for instance, as to where the crowd of people were located that you were able to observe with your naked eye.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Potocari. Round about here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you draw a circle --

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: The battery factory compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could put a "3" around there so that we know that when we have our record later that the "3" denotes where the crowd of people, the "2" where you fired, the "1" where you fired from, and the "X" where you initially started from?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, sir, about what time this was.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: About 1800 hours, about 18.30 hours thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't think we will need this exhibit any more. Thank you, Mr. Usher. And again, it's D151 for identification.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came back -- how long did you stay in that position?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Very short period of time. Just enough for us to pull out from that position because we were easily visible to the other side. And since those rockets had some sort of smoky gunpowder, when the firing took place, a large cloud of smoke is created. So we were quite a visible target to the opposite side. So what we usually did was to move away from the firing position as soon as possible after firing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Back to the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you report to anyone that you had accomplished that task that had been given to you by the communications officer or the duty officer from the Bratunac Brigade pursuant to what he claimed to have been General Mladic's order?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you fill out any report to send in, for instance, to the brigade so they could include this activity in their daily report?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No, that wasn't standard practice because I wasn't a military -- on personnel. I never did that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. After that, on the 11th, that same day, did anybody from the Drina Corps on the Main Staff or the Bratunac Brigade come by and --

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To discuss this matter?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after that event, did you carry out anything else, any other activities, on the 11th?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The day after Srebrenica fell, the 12th, any activities?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any orders?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any visitors from any commanders, including your own commander of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Mladic didn't stop by?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the 13th, did you receive any orders?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you issue any orders?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the 12th? I forgot to ask you whether you issued any orders.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 14th, the 15th, the 16th?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you -- what did your unit do during those days?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, most of them went home. They were being let go. We had a problem, and that was that when Srebrenica fell, all the mafioso types and thieves got going, and the furniture that the police had seized and was storing in warehouses, you had this -- and we also had an invasion of fleas and we all got fleas. It was impossible for anybody to imagine when I saw this. I found it astonishing. For example, when they took a couch, a settee and threw it into the warehouse, you could see this cloud of fleas coming up out of the sofa. You could see it with the naked eye.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask some concrete questions. On the 12th and 13th, did you go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you order any of your men to go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether anyone came by to take any of the trucks or any of the equipment to go to Potocari or anywhere else on the 12th or the 13th?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you had been the director of the Kaolin factory.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this period, did you maintain any offices in factory?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. My office was in the central part of the building which was separated from the army. You went in through the middle entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was there? What did you keep there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, we kept computers there, all the accounting service was there, accountancy and everything that we collected from the left and right wings that were occupied by the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have personnel working at the time in the administration building?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was somebody who was unfit for military service - he didn't have an eye, in fact - and he had the key. And my engineer who was the deputy assistant of the staff command or whatever it's called.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you visit the headquarters or visit your office during those days?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps, but that had nothing to do with the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, from the 6th through the 11th and 12th, and 13th, do you recall having gone to the factory, to the administration building for you -- you know, to visit your own offices?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps, but I don't remember. Probably I did, but I just don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you ever ran into anyone from the Main Staff of the Drina Corps such as Mladic, Beara, Krstic, Popovic, Kosoric, Jankovic of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No. And I don't know those people. I had a separate entrance which took me into the central part, and it was locked, and just those two men had the keys, the ones I mentioned, from the entrance gate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to go through a series of documents with you. And I'll start with -- I believe this has been marked as 149 for identification purposes. This is July 3, 1995. I think we're one off on the numbers in the exhibit list, Your Honours. We'll try to cure that. Do you see this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it says here that it's dated 3 July 1995. It's a request for equipment and materiel, and at the bottom, we see a Dragoslav Trisic. Do you see that name, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Major Trisic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could look at this list and tell us whether on July 3, 1995, whether any requests were made by Major Trisic that would be relevant to your particular unit?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No. There's nothing that was relevant to my unit here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Then we go on to the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is P406 dated 5 July 1995. It has been admitted already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can look at this, sir, is there -- and this is an order for active combat operations. If you go to the very last page, you'll see the name "Commander Colonel Vidoje Blagojevic." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you had an opportunity to look at this document yesterday, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to yesterday, had you seen this document?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything in this document --

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Or rather -- I beg your pardon. This is the order that I was shown earlier, before I gave my statement, if that's it, if that's the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. That was a statement you gave to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Prior to that, had you seen this document?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is there anything in this document, sir, that you see that relates to your rocket unit, the one that you were the komandir of?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. We'll go on to the next document. Let me show you what has been admitted into evidence as D131. It's dated July 12th, 1995. Now, this is -- again, do you see at the bottom of the page, it says "Major Dragoslav Trisic." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this would purport to be, would it not, a report to the Drina Corps command regarding consumption of materiel and equipment? Does it not state that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I suppose that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the date is 12 July 1995, correct, of this particular report?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we look at the bottom of the page, we notice that it was sent on the 12th of July, or at least that's what it would appear, at 1855 hours. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that would have been approximately - approximately - 24 hours after the firing of your rockets or whatever they were towards Pale?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything in this particular document, sir, that concerns --

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No. No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, I want to show you a rather interesting picture that has come -- that we have obtained from a video. It played some prominence in the Krstic trial. And it is P22. I don't believe it has been -- it might -- and the ERN number is 0291-7767. Okay. Could you please look at this document, sir -- or this photograph. First of all, do you know -- do you recognise what's in the picture? Do you recognise what it is?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: It's a truck with the launchers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know the size of these launchers?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this truck look anything familiar to what you had, what was available to you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, all those trucks are TAM 110s.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what about the launchers themselves, the rocket launchers? Does this truck look like it could have been one of yours?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, it looks like the truck, and it looks like the launchers, but they're all similar, trucks and launchers and similar, so I can't say whether it's actually that particular truck or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many trucks -- how many trucks did your unit have?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Two. One, the 110 and 150 TAM.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, this photograph was shown in the Krstic case as Exhibit 461. And during that time, he indicated that this was a -- and as we can see from the photograph itself provided to us from the Office of the Prosecution, this is an extract from the Petrovic footage, and it's dated 13 July 1995. My first question is, July 13, 1995, did you issue any orders for this -- for the truck that looked like this one that was in your unit to go anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No. I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Had I issued an order, there would be crew up on the truck. And here you see an empty truck. The launchers are empty; the truck's empty. So I'm not quite clear. I don't understand this, and I'm seeing this picture for the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what else would you expect to see as well?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Probably on that truck, for my unit, there were radars [as interpreted]. You couldn't see the launchers. That's why I very much doubt that that's the same truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be pulling --

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Not radars, tarpaulin. They were covered with a tarpaulin.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, not radar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would the truck be pulling anything as well?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it would be pulling the launchers, the 80-millimetre launcher, because there was an attached trailer. We didn't have any launchers that were operational, not on the truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, this exhibit as we can see was used in the Krstic trial as Exhibit Number 461, and I want to read a portion of his testimony with respect to this and get you to comment on it. It says -- he's being questioned by Mr. McCloskey: "Let's go to exhibit, I believe it is 461." I'm reading from the transcript page 4.866. The date is 28 June 2000. And line 3: "Let's go to the next exhibit. I believe it is 461. If you could put that on the ELMO. What's this?" And on the ELMO is placed, or we have marked as D150, and you could see the date, some time notated on the upper left-hand corner. Answer: "In time sequence, this is off of the same video, literally within a few seconds as the vehicles pass. This vehicle is in front of the -- I believe in front of the armoured personnel carrier. This is one of the two TAM rocket launchers that is assigned to the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade." Question: "How do you know that?" Answer: "The license plate, even on digital imagery or digital show is unclear. But we know from, again, the Bratunac Brigade records that there were two TAM rocket launchers assigned to the brigade." And then the next question is: "All right. Let's go to the next exhibit." So here, Mr. Butler assumes that this is one of the two trucks, albeit he cannot read the license plate. Is there anything that would -- in this picture that you can see that would at least help you to help us identify whether this was indeed the truck that belonged -- the TAM rocket launcher that belonged to the Bratunac Brigade on 13 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, it should have a trailer attached to the launchers because it was the main piece. And our truck had a tarpaulin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I didn't -- I don't know that our truck went out during those days. It had a tarpaulin and some other attachment. That's as far as I can notice. Otherwise, the trucks are all the same, and there were launchers in several units. Outside the Bratunac Brigade they had launchers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So this was not an unusual vehicle that only the Bratunac Brigade had?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And again, I'm reminded that this comes from -- this photograph comes from P22, chapter 16, page 4. But I believe that's what I'm told, so I'm putting it in the record. And I'm sure if I am incorrect, the Prosecution will correct us. Okay, thank you. Let me show you -- I'm reminded, Your Honour, that this may be a good time to take a short break. I do have one other matter left with the gentleman that may take -- that will take some time, not too much, but some time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Let's take a break. We'll resume at 10 minutes to 1.00. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, do you think we'll be able to have any more witnesses today, or should we plan for the next witness tomorrow, if anyone can estimate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm in the hands of Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Here's our schedule, Your Honour, and we're making some Herculean efforts to get as many people here as possible. In fact, I had issued an order myself to get somebody on the plane, two people. But we cannot unfortunately because of visa problems. This week, we will have six witnesses. The next two witnesses, I believe, can be handled in one day. I do have the following witness prepared, ready to go. So that's not a problem. And I seem to have additional energy today that will allow me to continue all the way through, even with another witness. So we can go forward. But it might be better, and I don't know how long the cross-examination will be, to just simply put the next witness off for tomorrow since we can finish probably both witnesses tomorrow, and that will be -- that's well in advance of the schedule. And it might -- because we will not be able to finish that witness. So we could keep the testimony all in one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We're fine with whatever -- we don't expect cross to be long at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. So there's a possibility for us to start the next witness today?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. We're ready. We're ready. I mean, again, I leave it to the Court and we'll see how it goes. But we will not be able to finish with that witness, cross and direct. But I don't suspect that that witness will take any longer than, say, a little bit over a session, direct and cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I anticipate these other witnesses taking much cross either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Let's -- if we have time, we will hear the next witness this morning. But if we don't have time, we have to leave him until tomorrow. Yes, we'll resume at 10 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Loncarevic, before we go on to the physical premises of your factory which was being used by the Bratunac Brigade as their headquarters, at least part of the administrative building, I want to go back to the actual footage where we saw this picture from, P22. And so we've asked the technical booth to assist us in playing a short portion of the Petrovic video.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You could play it back and...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Butler, on 28 June 2002, noted on page 4.866 that that vehicle was in front of the APC. Do you know what an APC is, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see an APC in that videoclip that we just saw?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No. I saw a police car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Perhaps we could play it one more time and maybe they can freeze the frame when we get to the APC.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I don't have anything. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, let's stop. I apologise. My screen isn't working, and I'm trying to figure this all out, and it's not terribly helpful when you're mechanically challenged to begin with. I'm pressing the wrong button. I apologise. If we could go slowly backwards. Okay, if we could stop right here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this vehicle? Do you know what this vehicle is?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I know it's an APC.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could move it backwards a little bit. Keep going. Keep going.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is relevant, Your Honours, for the following witness as well, so that's why. Okay, if we could -- if we could stop right there. Go further back, please. Okay, if you could stop right there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see that vehicle anywhere, assuming that this is the APC? The vehicle that would have looked like the one you had?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That will be it for the video. I just wanted to clarify the record with respect to Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I could show you what has been marked as D70 for identification purposes. We have seen it before, but it has not been tendered. It's D70 and D70.1, which is the text. If you could just look at those documents first. Do you recognise these documents, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The administration building of my company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, how do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course I recognise it. I built it. I supervised the construction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we could go through this document step by step so at least we have a pretty good indication of what is where, what's the ground floor? Which one of these? Which number? If you could take a look at the diagram itself, that might help.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, is that the ground floor? I want to start at the --

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No, this is the upper floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Which one is the ground floor? Perhaps we can go to where --

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: This is the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could just keep it on the ELMO there so we can all see it, what is number one? What does that stand for? What room is that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: This is the room where operational preparation took place. Just a moment. This is turned round. Where is the entrance? The staircase? Yes. So one is the operations preparation, and two is where the duty officer sat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, how do you get -- if you could use the pointer, please, and show us on the diagram where you would enter on that side.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it here? Yes. Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. Can you show us where you would enter in order to get to the operations room, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: This is where the operations -- you would enter here. That was the operations room, and then this was the room for the duty officer. And this is probably where the command held its meetings. And this here was a bathroom or a toilet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Just for the record, you are pointing to an entrance that was based at -- that is the left the room designated as "1." Now, is there -- how do you get to the first floor from the ground floor from this entrance?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: You go up these stairs here. You go upstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: To reach the command and Commander Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I want to go step by step, so let me walk you through this.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Hvala. Now, is the --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Excuse me. We're just having a little trouble following exactly where he's -- what he's talking about. I'm just wondering if maybe he can be directed to point to exactly where the command is, the duty officer. It's going quite quickly, and I don't believe he's pointing very specifically to the particular area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see there's no problem because all those rooms are numbered. Could we ask the witness to mark on this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. There's also an accompanying text that came in during the testimony, I believe it was with Nikolic. It wasn't actually tendered, but it was made reference to, just for the record, and it has been provided to the Prosecution months ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, Mr. Loncarevic, the Prosecution has never been to the building, so let's walk them through it. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you go through the entrance. Please show us where the entrance is and maybe put an "E" to it. So at least the Prosecution knows how to get into this building.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, you'd better say the Judges have never been to this building. That's more or less like it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. I trust that wasn't mischaracterising the evidence, though, but you're right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you please tell us where the stairway is to get to the first floor. Where are the stairs from that entrance?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, maybe you could put an "S" over there for "stairways" or "steps."

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we see that -- in this hallway between "E" and "S", there appears to be a wall. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have on the opposite side of "1" and "2," is that a wall separating?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: There's a wall separating the two offices.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, how would -- is that entire ground floor, can you go from, say, "E," once you walk into that entrance, can you walk all the way through to the other end of the building, the left side of the building?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What would you have to do in order to go to the opposite side of the building?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: You have to go out and go right through the compound and go in through the other entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, maybe you can look at the next diagram and show us where the entrance would be on the left side of the building. Maybe you can put "E2" over there so we know that this is a second entrance.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you put "2" next to the "E" as well, so as not to confuse us.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between the first entrance and the second entrance, "E2," is that portion of the ground floor, was that portion of the ground floor used by the Bratunac Brigade during that period?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which portion --

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: This was the dining room and the canteen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, which -- the dining room. Do you see a letter for the dining room?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. "K."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is "R"?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: "R" is the canteen or the lunchroom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If we go all the way to the left, could you please tell us what "3" and "4" are.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: When the company was operating, this was used by a doctor and a nurse. But now, it was the staff command in the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Do you know who was located there, which officers?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Milomir -- I can't remember his last name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. It's not important. Now, let's go to the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Milomir Stanojevic, that was his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go for the first floor. For those of us who are from the United States, this would be the second floor. Could you please try to locate where Colonel Blagojevic's office was located.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Number 7. Just a moment. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you wanted to go all the way -- well, why don't you show us. Where is Nikolic's, Momir Nikolic, where is his office located?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: It was upstairs. It was on the other one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I think it was 13.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So that's on the opposite side of the building?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: On the opposite of the building, on one corner, on the right-hand side, there was Mr. Blagojevic, and on the left-hand side, all the way there was Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now could --

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: The distance, let me tell you, was about 80 metres from one end to the other. The building is 80 metres long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you see through the hallway from one end to the other?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Because I put a partition there, two partitions, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why is that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: There were orders that partitions should be put there because computers were kept there. This was my office in the central part of the building, and the company archives, I mean, the factory, and these were very extensive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where the partitions were located. Could you show us and just put a "P," for partition, "1" and "2."

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Can this be "1." That was a partition. And on the other side, is it visible here? Yes. "2."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please put a "P" over there. A "P," the letter "P" so we know so as not to --

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: P2 or 2P?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You could put either one, P1 and P2, 2P and 1P. You choose.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who ordered -- who ordered the partition to be placed there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, simply, you know how it is when an army passes through a country, a territory, then there's a lot of suffering going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, to separate it off because there might be stealing. So people didn't need to see what was there, and neither did the workers need to see what was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did any members of the Main Staff or the Drina Corps or the Bratunac Brigade have access to that area that had been partitioned by you, where you had placed your equipment?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No. The only person who could go in was the assistant and the staff command, and he was an engineer of mine, and I allowed him to go there because he had an office up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any exceptions made, for instance, during those days when General Mladic was in town? I mean, he's a pretty big personality.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I didn't even know when he was in town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what about the compound itself? Outside the building, what access did the brigade have to the compound itself?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I would need to clarify. There was an agreement which I achieved that behind the administration building, the soldiers could not pass through. I had guards who were unfit for military service, and they were there all the time while the army, the soldiers, were using the administration building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there sufficient space around that area to park buses or trucks?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: They could park, but it wasn't allowed. And usually, what I wanted was respected. Commander Ognjenovic tried to challenge this, and so did Momir Nikolic. But the rest of the commanders, I don't know how many there were in the Bratunac Brigade, there was Ognjenovic and Momir Nikolic, Lieutenant Colonel or Colonel Nikolic. And they tried to rise above me and walk all over the factory any way they wanted. They wanted to go wherever they wanted throughout the whole compound, but I made it quite clear to them that I was in charge there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, the diagram that I showed you and that you have in front of you that -- and again, I want to correct the record, it should be marked as D152/1, with D152.1 the legend that goes with it, did you assist in any way in placing those numbers and identifying those rooms on this diagram?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: This was done by this engineer of mine with my approval because I knew about it. It was this engineer because he knew this better than I did since he had spent the whole war in that command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what about these numbers? Did you assist in locating the various rooms, who was where, who was occupying which offices?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. All the key places in that command, that was something I knew. And these are numbers I put there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to the best of your knowledge, does this diagram accurately reflect the outlay of the administration building of the Kaolin factory which was being used by the Bratunac Brigade at and around July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I guarantee that it's precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I have no further questions. I want to appreciate -- I want to thank you for your frank answers. The lawyer for Mr. Jokic may have some questions. The Prosecutor undoubtedly will have some, and perhaps even the Judges. If you can be as frank and forthright with them as you have been with me, I would most appreciate it. Thank you, again, for coming to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any questions, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'll have just a few questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examined by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Loncarevic.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm Branko Lukic, and together with Mr. Stojanovic who is not with us here today I defend Mr. Jokic before this Tribunal. I just have a few short questions for you to clarify certain points. You told us that apart from your military service, you did not have any military training in any formal terms. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever read instructions on the work of staffs?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the rules of service provide for the following: That the duty officer is an organ of the internal service?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know that the duty officer cannot issue orders?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your position, how often did you contact the duty officer at the headquarters of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I never contacted him. He did -- he contacted me when the need arose.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I do have just a few questions. Cross-examined by Ms. Issa:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to clarify a point, your commander was -- you were directly subordinated to Commander Blagojevic. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I thought that was the case. And I considered that to be so. However, in the statement that I read in the papers by Mico Gavric, he says that he was superior to me. I didn't know about that, to be quite frank. I didn't realise that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So are you saying that you don't really know who you're subordinated to? You don't know whether it's Commander Blagojevic or directly to Mico Gavric?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I thought that I was subordinate to Commander Blagojevic. I believed that to be the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you told us in the examination-in-chief that at some point you were involved in firing rockets pursuant to the -- to this order that you received. Did you see the artillery plan before you fired the rockets?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: What plan do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're not aware of an artillery plan that was in place at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the 5th July order, which I believe is Exhibit P406A for the record. You see you have a copy there in B/C/S which is signed by Commander Blagojevic. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like you to turn to paragraph 6.2. And if we can put that on the ELMO, please. It's at page 4. Now, that order at paragraph 6.2 states: "The 128-millimetre Rocket Launcher Platoon will provide support from the fire position in the Kaolin sector, at 0300 hours on 6 July 1995, it will fire four projectiles, [50-kilogram air bombs] on the Potocari sector [The school, the 11th of March factory, the Gracic hill, TT377, Kula, and Orici]." And it further states it will provide further support at the request of Captain Mico Gavric. Now, isn't that your platoon, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: The 128-millimetre launcher platoon, that's not something I had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But is there another rocket launcher platoon in the Bratunac Brigade besides the one that you commanded?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: There were 128-millimetre launchers, two of them, but before my arrival. That might have been in 1994 when they were dismounted. And on that truck, this bomb carrier was positioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, this as you can see at the very beginning, sir, is dated 5 July 1995. And in the paragraph 6.2, it says that the firing will occur on 6 July 1995 at 0300 hours. Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you see that it specifically refers to the rocket launcher platoon?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm telling you that there is no 128-millimetre platoon. There wasn't that kind of launcher at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Weren't you the only rocket launcher platoon in the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I say again that there wasn't a 128-millimetre launcher. Perhaps the commander didn't realise that. Forgot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're saying that perhaps the command forgot that there was no such platoon? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He didn't say "platoon." He's saying that the 128 millimetre did not exist with his platoon. That's what he's stating. So the Prosecutor, I know it's hard, but she should try to be fair with these witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Such platoon, I believe, is the 128-millimetre launcher platoon. Maybe you should make it more clear, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say, sir, that perhaps the command forgot, can you tell us what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, the 122 millimetres is an enormous flame as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What the question is, sir, and maybe this may clarify it, are you aware of any other rocket launcher platoon that is part of the Bratunac Brigade aside from yours?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No, there isn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So notwithstanding that the reference to the 128 millimetre, doesn't this appear to refer to your platoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection, it calls for speculation. Now she is trying to make the gentleman to be a liar when in fact he's saying he didn't have a 128. That's why he indicated that it wasn't part of his platoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, on this issue, I think the witness has the opportunity to answer this question by himself. Witness, would you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have said several times that we didn't have that type of weapon. It is "plamen and oganj." We had a bomb launcher, and this -- whereas this 128-millimetre rocket launcher it's an enormous calibre. It's a big-calibre weapon, and I have said already several times that we didn't have one like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You did have 50-kilogram air bombs, though. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you also told us that you weren't -- you're not aware of any other rocket launcher platoon besides yourself in the Bratunac Brigade. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I know there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So aside from that reference to the 128 millimetre, the rest of that paragraph would appear to refer to your platoon, would it not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to the 6 July 1995 daily combat report. It's at Exhibit P411A, English translation. If you look at paragraph 2, sir, of the 6 July daily combat report from the Bratunac Brigade addressed to the command of the Drina Corps, it states that: "Firing support against the set targets was provided by 70-millimetre shell launcher." In brackets, it says: "[School in Potocari, 11 of March factory, and the wide area of the village of Potocari]." Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not familiar with this. I see it, but we didn't target that. What date is this, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see at the top, sir, it says "6 July 1995."

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: What I remember is this: I just remember that on the 11th, that truck went to Pribicevac, not -- the seven bombs it had, it had seven bombs when the war was over. So what I'm saying -- what I'm telling you now, I stand by, and it is the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're saying you don't recall carrying out this order?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. He didn't say that. He said he didn't carry out the order, not that he didn't recall, as if it was carried out and somehow now he has a lapse of memory. There's a big distinction and it's a total mischaracterisation of his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, you may rephrase your question to make sure whether it's a recall or just carrying out the order.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Well, I took that from his previous answer, Your Honour, where he says, "What I remember is this: I just remember," and he continues. But I certainly can rephrase that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember carrying out such an order, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible that you did carry out such an order given what's contained in the daily combat report?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't think that is possible, no, to the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say "to the best of your recollection," is it possible you simply don't recall?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I ought not to remember. But as I say, the only seven bombs that I had, I handed over -- I handed back after the war, those same seven.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember because I had a terrible accident in 2002. I had major surgery on my abdomen. I had 11 broken ribs. And I was in a coma for many days. I have an iron rod in my arm. But as far as I remember, I didn't work with the bomb or rocket launcher at all. Grenade launcher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, maybe we can just move into -- go into another area. Are you aware, sir, that in Vlasenica there was a corps artillery group?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the corps had -- the Drina Corps artillery group had rockets?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of any other group that had rockets?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I did see those launchers round about, but I don't know who they belonged to. I know that there were some -- the 57-millimetre ones, I would see in Vlasenica. As to the larger rockets, I never saw them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you've seen rockets in Vlasenica. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: But they're the small ones, 57-millimetre ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when was that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: That was -- I think we went to copy one like that, to copy that launcher, and that's when I might have seen it, to make these devices from the launchers. And that's when I saw them first and never again. I saw one actually that the Muslims captured, seized; I don't know who from. And then half a year later I saw it in Srebrenica. But these launchers had been made, and you could see them everywhere on the battlefields.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, that there were rockets that were launched -- into the enclave on the 6th of July according to the UNMO reports?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that the UNMO also reported that seven rockets were launched or were used by the Bosnian Serb Army on the 7th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that on the 10th of July, UNMO reported that eight rockets were fired in the direction of Srebrenica in the morning?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the afternoon on that same day, are you aware that rockets, according to the UNMO report, were launched into the town?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I want to stick with the Document P406, start there. You were shown paragraph 6.2. Now, in this particular order, does it say anything about 70-millimetre shells being launched by your platoon, assuming that this was your platoon, which is being insinuated by the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: What point do you mean? Which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 6.2, where it says "tasks."

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can see here that there's a -- where it says: "Four projectiles, 50-kilogram air bombs." That's what I see. And that's what I had. I had the same thing in my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is that the same as the 70-millimetre shells that are being referred to?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you said that you started, or the platoon had seven grenades or seven launchers before the attack on Srebrenica. And you still had the seven at the end of the events surrounding Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I claim and guarantee that to be true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. In spite of your accident. In spite of the accident that you had?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did anybody come over with any additional grenades during that period for you to use?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. No. At least, I don't know. I'm not aware about that, of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you have any connection in a sense of working with the Drina Corps during those days?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you have any reason to be in Vlasenica and to speak with any of your counterparts there that might have been working with artillery, rocket launchers, or what have you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: When I mentioned Vlasenica, that was part of the job in 1994 when we made the shelter for us so that we could come out of the trenches to make those launchers. So quite simply, to see how they were assembled, made and assembled on to the trucks. Nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, we know from testimony that Colonel Blagojevic came to the command at or around May 25th, 1995. Could you please tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, is this question within the scope of the cross?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It is. It's very much in the scope. If I can be allowed first to ask the question, and then I'll -- I think from hearing the entire question, it will become relevant. Well, let me lay the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ask your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From May 1995, May 25, 1995 when Colonel Blagojevic assumed the position as commander of the Bratunac Brigade to the beginning of activities with respect to Srebrenica, did he come over to where your unit was to inspect and see what equipment was there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS LONCAREVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That is outside the scope of the cross-examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe that following-up question will put us back into the scope.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It was being suggested to you that you perhaps were mistaken or maybe even fabricating when you said that the commander didn't know about you not having a 128, going back to paragraph 6.2, a 128-millimetre rocket launcher platoon. And you said the commander might have mistaken. Is it possible, sir, that because he was a new commander, he didn't actually know what your unit had?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: This is totally argumentative and leading. I mean, Mr. Karnavas is not testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the suggestion is that the commander knew. We have testimony that he arrived shortly thereafter. I'm entitled to elicit information as to whether the commander visited that unit and knew what was available because perhaps there were some mistakes. That's all I'm trying to get at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, since we have very little time available for this sitting, we would like to hear the answer from the witness. Then, I believe that we could wind up this redirect as soon as possible. Witness, you may answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps Commander Blagojevic saw those devices because they were handmade devices, for the first time. Now, as far as I know, and I've known him since we were children, he's an engineer's man. I know his entire training, how he grew up, and all the rest of it. So he couldn't have known, if he was an engineer's man, he couldn't have known what it was because I wasn't well-versed in things like that either. I was seeing that for the first time, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's all I wanted to get out, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps it's a mere coincidence, but we have over the last week have seen several times where there are efforts going beyond the scope. This is a very serious rule in this -- in any, as you know, because it requires us to try to anticipate that and keeps opening the door back and forth. And that's clearly designed to leave us with that, and I don't know if it was done on purpose or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we need to be very strict upon that particular rule because then it requires us to change our whole viewpoint. And I think you can see we're trying to be as restrictive and as targeted as we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I listened very carefully to the cross. Doors are being opened. I'm trying to slam them. And I must be frank: At times, I think we're having a finishing school in this courtroom. I think this is well within the scope. A door was opened, and I'm anticipating the closing argument that they will have. I'm entitled to close that door. I'm entitled to give this gentleman an opportunity to give a full answer. And then conclusions can be drawn from there. But I take exception to what Mr. McCloskey's saying that somehow I'm trying to open up these new areas and leave them hanging. If they feel that I've gone into an area that is outside the scope, I welcome the opportunity for them to reopen their cross-examination. I don't have a problem with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think this Bench has warned you many times before that redirect should be strictly within the cross-examination. And whether it's within the scope or not I think is the decision made by the Bench rather than by you yourself. There's a rule that no matter what kind of decision the parties must obey, that is saying that when the Judges stands, nobody will sit. I hope in the future, if you have any questions to ask, you must do it in your direct rather than leave it until the redirect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I take --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: This is what I'm going to say at this late hour because we're five minutes past the time. I'm not going to debate on this issue with anybody. And at this stage, are there any documents to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. D149, the request for equipment and materiel of 3 July 1995; D150, the image from the Krstic exhibit, which is P46, where we made reference to the content from Butler, from his footnotes; I believe it's D151, the map that was marked by this witness; D152/1 and D152.1/1, which are the blueprint and the legend that goes with it that was -- that we brought in during I believe the Nikolic testimony and the gentleman authenticated here today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any objections, Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Those documents are admitted into the evidence. I hope after this sitting, the Defence counsel could work with the Court Deputy to straighten out the numbers of those documents because we have different numbers than the sheets you furnished to us at the beginning of the trial. Are there any documents on the Prosecution side to tender?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. When our sitting is adjourned, the usher will show you out of the room. We wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 13th day of May, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.51 p.m.,
